_comment: EUR per kWh. 'solar' is NOT zero: self-consumed PV forgoes the feed-in tariff, so its marginal cost is the feed-in rate (or LCOE if you prefer the full-cost view).

solar-de-feed-in.label: Germany PV self-consumption, opportunity cost = feed-in tariff <=10 kWp (Aug 2026-Jan 2027)

solar-de-lcoe.label: Germany small rooftop PV (<=30 kWp) LCOE, mid-range of 6.3-14.4 ct/kWh (Fraunhofer ISE, Jul 2024)

cloud_inference_co2_estimate._comment: *** ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE ESTIMATE, NOT A MEASUREMENT. *** No cloud AI provider publishes energy per token, so unlike every other number in this file this one cannot be sourced to a vendor figure -- it is reconstructed from published per-query estimates divided by an assumed response length. Treat it as accurate to within roughly a factor of 3, and do not quote it as a fact about any specific provider. Full derivation, sources and error bars: docs/CO2_ESTIMATE.md.
cloud_inference_co2_estimate.wh_per_mtok_it_source: ESTIMATE: ~0.25-0.3 Wh per typical LLM chat query (Google, 'Measuring the environmental impact of delivering AI products', 2025, median Gemini text prompt 0.24 Wh; Epoch AI 2025 GPT-4o-class estimate ~0.3 Wh/query) divided by an assumed ~500 output tokens per query => ~0.5 Wh per 1k tokens => 500 Wh per 1M tokens. Older widely-cited figures (de Vries, Joule 2023, ~2.9 Wh/query) would put this ~6x higher; see docs/CO2_ESTIMATE.md.
cloud_inference_co2_estimate.pue_label: PUE 1.15 (hyperscale fleet average; Google reports ~1.09, Microsoft ~1.18, AWS ~1.15)
cloud_inference_co2_estimate.pue_source: ESTIMATE: midpoint of the fleet-wide PUE figures the three largest cloud providers publish in their annual sustainability reports.
cloud_inference_co2_estimate.confidence: LOW -- good to roughly a factor of 3 either way. It is a magnitude, not a measurement.
cloud_inference_co2_estimate.basis: ~0.25-0.3 Wh per published LLM query / ~500 output tokens per query, x datacentre PUE, x grid carbon intensity.

us-avg.label: US national average grid mix (approx.)
us-avg.source: ESTIMATE: ~0.85 lb CO2/kWh, the commonly-cited EPA eGRID-class US national average; not re-verified against the latest eGRID release.

us-gas-heavy.label: US datacentre region with a gas-dominated mix (ERCOT/PJM-class, approx.)
us-gas-heavy.source: ESTIMATE: a modern combined-cycle gas plant emits roughly 350-400 gCO2/kWh at the plant; a grid where gas sets most of the marginal generation lands somewhat above that. Representative of the 'AI industry runs on gas' framing, not a figure published for any named balancing authority.

de-grid.label: German grid mix -- the same-grid comparison (approx.)
de-grid.source: Same figure as the grid-de-household tariff above; use it to compare cloud vs. local hardware on the SAME grid, isolating the efficiency difference from the grid-mix difference.
